about.author: Author: {author}. Built with AI assistance.
about.components_intro: Voxprint stands on the following open-source projects and models. Thank you to their authors!
about.concept: Voxprint grew out of a search for a truly one-button voice-cloning tool. The tools we found needed a command line, manual setup of components or hand-prepared files, or covered only a single step. Voxprint covers the whole path: from a voice recording and a text file to ready output files you can load into a neural network. Your effort is minimal: read a text aloud and attach two files. It was built jointly by a human and an AI - an honest attempt. It is economical: models already downloaded by other apps are reused instead of being downloaded again. Windows comes first, other operating systems later.
about.lgpl: Qt/PySide6 is used under the LGPL-3.0, unmodified and dynamically linked. In the folder-type build you can replace its libraries.
about.notices_missing: The notices file was not found next to the program.
about.privacy: Responsible use: use a voice only with its owner's explicit permission and respect the voice's licence; no impersonation, fraud or misleading content; label synthetic speech where required. Recordings and results stay on this computer; the program sends nothing to the internet except downloading models and checking for updates.
about.requirements: Requirements: Windows 11 26H2 is optimal; an NVIDIA graphics card with 16 GB of video memory is recommended.
about.step1: Read a known text aloud and record it (5-15 minutes).
about.step2: Choose the recording and the text file.
about.step3: Voxprint aligns the text to the audio with a neural forced aligner and cuts it into clean fragments - the dataset.
about.step4: Optionally it trains a small voice adapter (LoRA) on your graphics card.
about.step5: Optionally it merges the adapter into a universal model (~4 GB) that works in any app running Qwen3-TTS.
about.title: About Voxprint AI Audiobook Builder
about.what: Voxprint turns a recording of a voice (yours, or of a person who has given permission) into a voice for Qwen3-TTS. Everything happens on your computer.

ui.privacy_text:
A voice is personal data and a personality right of its owner. Use a voice only with the explicit permission of the person it belongs to, and respect the voice's licence (shown in voice.json and in “My voices”; for example CC BY-NC means personal, non-commercial use only).

Do not use synthetic speech to impersonate anyone, to deceive or defraud, or to produce misleading content. Label synthetic speech where this is required. You are responsible for the lawful use of the voices and audio you create.

Recordings, text and the finished voice are stored only on your computer; the program sends nothing to the internet except downloading models and checking for updates.

warn.very_low_vram: Video memory is low: a lighter model is used, voice quality may be lower.
warn.voice_not_registered: The voice was saved, but could not be added to “My voices” automatically - import the output folder there.
asr.choose_script: Script (optional): the text that was read aloud…
asr.script_none: (no script: the speech is recognised without one)
auto.button_tip: Selects every recommended automatic option and downloads the models they need
auto.hint: One click selects every automatic step that exists: text preparation, AI clean-up of typos, the voice check and the A/B comparison. The models they need are downloaded once. Alignment and the audio checks are always on. Single options can still be changed in their windows.
auto.done_none: All recommended options are selected; the models they need are already downloaded.
auto.done: Done: {n} model(s) downloaded. All recommended options are selected.
auto.failed: Download failed: {error}. The options are selected; press the button again to continue.
narr.pauses_hint: Silence of a measured length is inserted after every comma, sentence, ellipsis, dash, paragraph, scene break and chapter, independent of how the voice model phrases the text, so the pauses are clearly audible. "Normal" is a little longer than the earlier narration. Changing it later only re-joins the audio when the text pieces stay the same.
ui.voice_type_hint: The voice type goes into voice.json and into the name of the trained voice's folder (for example anna_male).
ui.voice_type_suggest: Suggested from the recording's pitch: {type} (about {hz} Hz). Change it if this is wrong.
err.model_hash: The downloaded model {short} failed the integrity check (SHA-256) and was deleted. Please try again.
err.translate_failed: The translation failed. Please try again; finished parts are kept.
err.translate_model: The translation model {source} to {target} is not downloaded yet. Press Download in the translation section.
err.translate_pair: Translation from {source} to {target} is not available. Supported languages: English, Russian, German.
err.translate_source: The language of the book could not be detected, so it cannot be translated. Supported source languages: English, Russian, German.
narr.translate_check: Translate the book before narrating, to:
narr.translate_needs: Needs a one-time download of the translation model(s), about {size} MB.
narr.translate_note: Automatic machine translation: quality varies - names, idioms, dialogue and long sentences can come out wrong, and poems lose their rhyme. It runs offline on this computer (graphics card if there is one, otherwise the processor; a long book can take a while). The translated text is saved next to the audiobook as translation_xx.txt: read it, edit it and start again to narrate your edited text. You are responsible for having the right to translate and narrate the text (copyright and licences); this is not legal advice.
narr.translate_pivot: {source} to {target} goes through English: slower and less accurate.
narr.translate_same: The book is already in this language - nothing to translate.
narr.translate_unsupported: Translation from this language is not available (detected: {source}). Supported: English, Russian, German.
narr.translate_voice: The selected voice speaks {voice}; the book will be narrated in {target}. A voice of the target language usually sounds best.
